AgentTrustState.description:
Whether the server still trusts an agent's credentials. Deliberately
separate from AgentStatus: online/offline says whether the machine is
reachable, trust says whether we will act on its behalf at all.

active      -> normal operation
quarantined -> authenticates, but receives no commands and may not submit
               results; reversible by an operator
revoked     -> credentials fail authentication entirely; terminal — the
               machine must re-enroll under a new identity
AgentTrustState.title: AgentTrustState

AlertEventType.description: Immutable lifecycle transitions and technician actions (#44).
AlertEventType.title: AlertEventType

AlertState.description:
Lifecycle state for one deduplicated monitoring alert.

#43 drives ``open`` and automatic ``resolved`` transitions. The
``acknowledged`` value is reserved for #44's role-gated technician action
so mixed server versions share one stable database contract.
AlertState.title: AlertState

CheckResultStatus.description:
Evaluation outcome for one check on one agent.

``unknown`` is distinct from ``ok``: it means the check could not be
evaluated (the agent did not report, or the metric was unavailable), which
a technician must be able to tell apart from a passing check.
CheckResultStatus.title: CheckResultStatus

CommandDetailOut.description: Full command record: signed envelope evidence plus the bounded result.
CommandDetailOut.title: CommandDetailOut

CommandHistoryItemOut.description:
One row of an endpoint's command history.

`status` is the effective status: a stored queued/dispatched command whose
expires_at has passed is reported as expired even before the next agent
heartbeat persists that transition, so operators never see an expired
command still presented as pending work.
CommandHistoryItemOut.title: CommandHistoryItemOut

detail.description: Human-readable message, or a coded object. Clients branch on `code`, never on message text.

InstalledUpdate.description: One update already installed on the endpoint (issue #51).
InstalledUpdate.title: InstalledUpdate

InventoryOut.description: The current inventory for one agent: at most one row per section.
InventoryOut.title: InventoryOut

InventorySection.description: Section names. Later inventory issues add members here, not schemas.
InventorySection.title: InventorySection

InventorySectionOut.description: One stored section, newest first in operator views.
InventorySectionOut.title: InventorySectionOut

InventorySectionStatus.description:
Why a section looks the way it does.

``ok``                collected completely.
``partial``           collected, but bounded away — some rows are missing.
``unavailable``       the platform supports this but collection failed.
``unsupported``       the platform cannot report it at all.
``permission_denied`` the platform supports it and it exists, but the agent
                      lacks the rights to read it.

``permission_denied`` is separated from ``unavailable`` because the two
call for different responses. An unavailable section is a transient fault
to retry; a denied one is a fixable deployment problem — the agent is not
running with the privileges its collectors need — and would otherwise hide
inside generic failures forever. BitLocker is the first collector that can
hit it, since its cmdlets require elevation.
InventorySectionStatus.title: InventorySectionStatus

MissingUpdate.description:
One applicable-but-not-installed update the scan found (issue #51).

``title`` is the only field a row cannot be reported without; everything
else is ``None`` when Windows Update did not supply it, never guessed.
MissingUpdate.title: MissingUpdate

RebootCauseOut.description:
Why a restart is pending, plus correlated update inventory.

``verdict`` is categorical and derives only from ``sources``. The update
lists stay correlation evidence and never become a cause. Agents that
predate reboot-source reporting send no sources and yield ``unknown``.
RebootCauseOut.title: RebootCauseOut

RebootSourcesOut.description:
Which Windows reboot-required registry sources the endpoint reported.

Only ``windows_update`` means an installed update is waiting on a restart.
``pending_file_rename_count`` is a count and never a path: the paths behind
it routinely contain user names, and this payload is meant to stay safe to
forward to alert email and third-party webhooks. It is best-effort and null
when unavailable.
RebootSourcesOut.title: RebootSourcesOut

Queue a command for an agent, signed so the agent can verify authenticity.

The acting operator is recorded in the audit event, so the tamper-evident
log answers not just *what* ran but *who* ordered it.
